result.topic_en: Orthogonality relations for spherical-harmonic-type functions f^m(p,P): the integral of the product of two such functions vanishes for unequal orders and gives a multiple of f(P,P') for equal orders.
result.transcription:
$\int f^{m}(p.P).f^{n}(p.P').d\mu = 0$
wenn $m$ und $n$ ungleich sind hingegen
$\int f^{m}(p,P).f^{m}(p,P')\,d\mu = \frac{1}{(2m+1)\pi} f(P,P')$

methods.what: Orthogonality of spherical-harmonic-type functions of different orders under integration over the sphere
Integral of the product of two same-order functions, integrated over the variable point p, equals a normalised function of the two fixed points P and P'

items.english: The integral of f^m(p,P)·f^n(p,P') dμ equals 0 when m and n are unequal.
On the other hand, the integral of f^m(p,P)·f^m(p,P') dμ equals f(P,P') divided by (2m+1)π.
